From a16d1ec4dd0cdcf689f324adde6067083bce9099 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Zide Chen <zide.chen@intel.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 10:40:49 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] perf/x86/intel/uncore: Fix die ID init and look up bugs

In snbep_pci2phy_map_init(), in the nr_node_ids > 8 path,
uncore_device_to_die() may return -1 when all CPUs associated
with the UBOX device are offline.

Remove the WARN_ON_ONCE(die_id == -1) check for two reasons:

- The current code breaks out of the loop. This is incorrect because
  pci_get_device() does not guarantee iteration in domain or bus order,
  so additional UBOX devices may be skipped during the scan.

- Returning -EINVAL is incorrect, since marking offline buses with
  die_id == -1 is expected and should not be treated as an error.

Separately, when NUMA is disabled on a NUMA-capable platform,
pcibus_to_node() returns NUMA_NO_NODE, causing uncore_device_to_die()
to return -1 for all PCI devices.  As a result,
spr_update_device_location(), used on Intel SPR and EMR, ignores the
corresponding PMON units and does not add them to the RB tree.

Fix this by using uncore_pcibus_to_dieid(), which retrieves topology
from the UBOX GIDNIDMAP register and works regardless of whether NUMA
is enabled in Linux.  This requires snbep_pci2phy_map_init() to be
added in spr_uncore_pci_init().

Keep uncore_device_to_die() only for the nr_node_ids > 8 case, where
NUMA is expected to be enabled.

Fixes: 9a7832ce3d92 ("perf/x86/intel/uncore: With > 8 nodes, get pci bus die id from NUMA info")
Fixes: 65248a9a9ee1 ("perf/x86/uncore: Add a quirk for UPI on SPR")
Signed-off-by: Zide Chen <zide.chen@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Dapeng Mi <dapeng1.mi@linux.intel.com>
Tested-by: Steve Wahl <steve.wahl@hpe.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260313174050.171704-4-zide.chen@intel.com

diff --git a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_snbep.c b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_snbep.c
index 0a1d08136cc1..a4b337bf83c0 100644
--- a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_snbep.c
+++ b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_snbep.c
@@ -1459,13 +1459,7 @@ static int snbep_pci2phy_map_init(int devid, int nodeid_loc, int idmap_loc, bool
 			}
 
 			map->pbus_to_dieid[bus] = die_id = uncore_device_to_die(ubox_dev);
-
 			raw_spin_unlock(&pci2phy_map_lock);
-
-			if (WARN_ON_ONCE(die_id == -1)) {
-				err = -EINVAL;
-				break;
-			}
 		}
 	}
 
@@ -6420,7 +6414,7 @@ static void spr_update_device_location(int type_id)
 
 	while ((dev = pci_get_device(PCI_VENDOR_ID_INTEL, device, dev)) != NULL) {
 
-		die = uncore_device_to_die(dev);
+		die = uncore_pcibus_to_dieid(dev->bus);
 		if (die < 0)
 			continue;
 
@@ -6444,6 +6438,11 @@ static void spr_update_device_location(int type_id)
 
 int spr_uncore_pci_init(void)
 {
+	int ret = snbep_pci2phy_map_init(0x3250, SKX_CPUNODEID, SKX_GIDNIDMAP, true);
+
+	if (ret)
+		return ret;
+
 	/*
 	 * The discovery table of UPI on some SPR variant is broken,
 	 * which impacts the detection of both UPI and M3UPI uncore PMON.
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore.c b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore.c
index 786bd51a0d89..e9cc1ba921c5 100644
--- a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore.c
+++ b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore.c
@@ -67,6 +67,7 @@ int uncore_die_to_segment(int die)
 	return bus ? pci_domain_nr(bus) : -EINVAL;
 }
 
+/* Note: This API can only be used when NUMA information is available. */
 int uncore_device_to_die(struct pci_dev *dev)
 {
 	int node = pcibus_to_node(dev->bus);

## Summary of Modifications

### Files Modified

1. **`arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_snbep.c`**  
   - **`snbep_pci2phy_map_init()`** (line ~1459): Removed the `WARN_ON_ONCE(die_id == -1)` check and the associated `err = -EINVAL; break;` statement. Now the loop continues to scan all UBOX devices, even if `uncore_device_to_die()` returns -1 (e.g., all CPUs on the device’s node are offline). This prevents incorrect early termination of the PCI device scan and avoids treating expected offline buses as errors.  
   - **`spr_update_device_location()`** (line ~6420): Replaced `uncore_device_to_die(dev)` with `uncore_pcibus_to_dieid(dev->bus)`. The former relies on Linux NUMA information (`pcibus_to_node()`) and fails when NUMA is disabled; the latter reads the hardware GIDNIDMAP register to determine the die ID independently, fixing the issue where PMON units were ignored on NUMA-disabled systems.  
   - **`spr_uncore_pci_init()`** (line ~6438): Added a call to `snbep_pci2phy_map_init()` to build the mapping from PCI bus to die ID via the GIDNIDMAP register. This mapping is required by `uncore_pcibus_to_dieid()` and was not previously initialized in this function, causing it to fail.

2. **`arch/x86/events/intel/uncore.c`**  
   - **`uncore_device_to_die()`** (line ~70): Added a comment clarifying that this function can only be used when NUMA information is available (`pcibus_to_node()` returns a valid node). This documents the limitation that motivated the change in `spr_update_device_location()`.

### Relationships Between Changes

The modifications in `uncore_snbep.c` directly address two distinct bugs:

- The removal of the `WARN_ON_ONCE` + `break` in `snbep_pci2phy_map_init()` eliminates an incorrect early exit that could skip later UBOX devices and treats -1 (expected for offline buses) as an error.  
- The switch from `uncore_device_to_die()` to `uncore_pcibus_to_dieid()` in `spr_update_device_location()` fixes a failure when NUMA is disabled. However, `uncore_pcibus_to_dieid()` requires the mapping table built by `snbep_pci2phy_map_init()`, which was missing from `spr_uncore_pci_init()`. The new call to `snbep_pci2phy_map_init()` inside `spr_uncore_pci_init()` ensures that mapping is created before it is used.

The comment added in `uncore.c` serves as documentation, explaining why `uncore_device_to_die()` cannot be used in the NUMA-disabled scenario, reinforcing the rationale for the replacement in `spr_update_device_location()`.

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications in Each File

1. **arch/x86/events/intel/uncore.c**  
   - Added a comment to the `uncore_device_to_die()` function clarifying that it can only be used when NUMA information is available.

2. **arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_snbep.c**  
   - **`snbep_pci2phy_map_init()`** (line ~1462): Removed the `WARN_ON_ONCE(die_id == -1)` check along with its associated `err = -EINVAL` and `break`. Previously, when a UBOX device had all CPUs offline (die_id = -1), the WARN triggered an error exit that could skip scanning further UBOX devices (since `pci_get_device` does not guarantee order). The change treats die_id == -1 as a normal condition and no longer breaks the loop early.  
   - **`spr_update_device_location()`** (line ~6417): Replaced `uncore_device_to_die(dev)` with `uncore_pcibus_to_dieid(dev->bus)`. The old function uses `pcibus_to_node()`, which returns `NUMA_NO_NODE` when NUMA is disabled, leading to die_id = -1 and skipping PMON units. The new function reads die ID from the UBOX GIDNIDMAP register, working regardless of NUMA being enabled.  
   - **`spr_uncore_pci_init()`** (line ~6441): Added a call to `snbep_pci2phy_map_init(0x3250, SKX_CPUNODEID, SKX_GIDNIDMAP, true)` at the beginning. This builds the PCI bus-to-die mapping needed by `uncore_pcibus_to_dieid()`. Previously this mapping was not initialized for SPR/EMR platforms, causing the lookup to fail.

### Relationships Between Changes

- The comment in `uncore_device_to_die()` documents its NUMA dependency, which explains why it fails when NUMA is disabled—motivating the switch to `uncore_pcibus_to_dieid()` in the second file.  
- The removal of the WARN_ON in `snbep_pci2phy_map_init()` fixes a separate bug where die_id = -1 (from offline CPUs) caused premature loop termination and error return. This change is independent but related to robustness of die ID handling.  
- The call to `snbep_pci2phy_map_init()` in `spr_uncore_pci_init()` is required because `uncore_pcibus_to_dieid()` relies on the mapping table built by that function. Without this call, the new die ID lookup would fail entirely.  
- Together, these modifications ensure correct die ID initialization and lookup for all scenarios: (a) offline CPUs on large systems (>8 nodes), (b) systems with NUMA disabled, and (c) Intel SPR/EMR platforms where the UBOX GIDNIDMAP register must be used.

### Summary of Modifications

#### Modifications in Each File

1. **`arch/x86/events/intel/uncore.c`**  
   - Added a comment above `uncore_device_to_die()`:  
     `/* Note: This API can only be used when NUMA information is available. */`

2. **`arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_snbep.c`**  
   - **In `snbep_pci2phy_map_init()`**: Removed the `WARN_ON_ONCE(die_id == -1)` check and its associated `break` and `err = -EINVAL` assignment. Previously, if `uncore_device_to_die()` returned -1 (e.g., when all CPUs for a UBOX device were offline), the function would break out of the loop prematurely and return an error. This was incorrect because `pci_get_device()` does not guarantee iteration order, so subsequent UBOX devices could be skipped. The removal treats offline buses with `die_id == -1` as a normal condition rather than an error.  
   - **In `spr_update_device_location()`**: Replaced `uncore_device_to_die(dev)` with `uncore_pcibus_to_dieid(dev->bus)`. The former fails when NUMA is disabled because `pcibus_to_node()` returns `NUMA_NO_NODE`, causing the die ID to be -1 for all devices. The latter reads the UBOX GIDNIDMAP register to obtain the die ID, which works regardless of whether NUMA support is enabled in Linux.  
   - **In `spr_uncore_pci_init()`**: Added a call to `snbep_pci2phy_map_init(0x3250, SKX_CPUNODEID, SKX_GIDNIDMAP, true)` at the beginning, with a check for the return value. This builds the PCI-to-physical mapping (including reading GIDNIDMAP) before `spr_update_device_location()` uses `uncore_pcibus_to_dieid()`. Without this initialization, the new lookup would not have the necessary data.

- The comment in `uncore.c` warns that `uncore_device_to_die()` is only valid when NUMA information is available, directly explaining why the bug occurs when NUMA is disabled.
- The removal of the `WARN_ON_ONCE` and early `break` in `snbep_pci2phy_map_init()` fixes a separate bug where offline CPUs incorrectly stopped scanning of other UBOX devices, and it aligns with the new expectation that `die_id == -1` is a normal condition.
- The replacement in `spr_update_device_location()` is the core fix for the NUMA-disabled scenario, switching from a NUMA-dependent function to a register-based lookup.
- The addition of `snbep_pci2phy_map_init()` in `spr_uncore_pci_init()` enables the register-based lookup to work by populating the internal mapping structures. Without this, `uncore_pcibus_to_dieid()` would fail because it relies on data initialized by `snbep_pci2phy_map_init()`.
- Together, these changes ensure that die ID resolution works correctly on Intel SPR/EMR platforms whether NUMA is enabled or disabled, and that the PCI scanning logic does not terminate prematurely due to offline CPUs.

        Root cause:
        uncore_device_to_die() relies on pcibus_to_node() which returns NUMA_NO_NODE when NUMA is disabled, causing die ID lookup to fail with -1 and skip PMON units. Additionally, in the path for >8 nodes, offline CPUs cause the same -1 return, and the flawed error handling with WARN_ON_ONCE and break prematurely stops scanning other UBOX devices.
        
        Commit message:
        perf/x86/intel/uncore: Fix die ID init and look up bugs

In snbep_pci2phy_map_init(), in the nr_node_ids > 8 path,
uncore_device_to_die() may return -1 when all CPUs associated
with the UBOX device are offline.

Remove the WARN_ON_ONCE(die_id == -1) check for two reasons:

- The current code breaks out of the loop. This is incorrect because
  pci_get_device() does not guarantee iteration in domain or bus order,
  so additional UBOX devices may be skipped during the scan.

- Returning -EINVAL is incorrect, since marking offline buses with
  die_id == -1 is expected and should not be treated as an error.

Separately, when NUMA is disabled on a NUMA-capable platform,
pcibus_to_node() returns NUMA_NO_NODE, causing uncore_device_to_die()
to return -1 for all PCI devices.  As a result,
spr_update_device_location(), used on Intel SPR and EMR, ignores the
corresponding PMON units and does not add them to the RB tree.

Fix this by using uncore_pcibus_to_dieid(), which retrieves topology
from the UBOX GIDNIDMAP register and works regardless of whether NUMA
is enabled in Linux.  This requires snbep_pci2phy_map_init() to be
added in spr_uncore_pci_init().

Keep uncore_device_to_die() only for the nr_node_ids > 8 case, where
NUMA is expected to be enabled.
